FormNodeBinding.usage: Use for an injected binding, directive query, or integration callback. It describes the rendered binding, including outputs and host access; it is not a form node.

FieldNode.usage: Use for inputs or helpers that accept a field with a known value type. A bare `FieldNode` accepts unspecified field values; prefer factory inference when declaring the field itself.

FieldApi.usage: Use for helpers that operate on field state and actions without accepting a node declaration. A field's `$api` additionally has the callable signal contract described by [`CallableNodeApi`](./callable-node-api.md).
FieldApi.description: State, value views, navigation, and operations available on a field node.

FieldOptions.usage: Use when sharing field configuration. Let `field()` infer value and owner types for ordinary declarations instead of annotating every options object. The `configure` callback receives this instance’s typed, collision-safe API synchronously once. See [configuration lifecycle and sibling rules](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md).
FieldOptions.description: Value, validation, interaction, and ownership configuration for field().

ValidatorOptions.usage: Use for reusable custom validator configuration. Built-in validators expose their concrete options inline; consult each validator for supported value and context types.

FormNodeDirective.usage: Use this type for a template-reference or view query. The same exported name is also the runtime directive imported in Angular components; use a normal import when adding it to `imports`.
FormNodeDirective.description: The public instance type of the [formNode] Angular directive.

ObservableLike.usage: Use for an async source compatible with the library without depending on RxJS types. Honor subscription cleanup so cancelled validation stops its work.

ObserverLike.usage: Use when implementing an observable-like validator source. Deliver values and completion or errors according to the observer contract.

SubscriptionLike.usage: Return this cleanup handle from an observable-like source. The validation pipeline uses it to release obsolete work.

GroupNode.usage: Use for a structural group with no independent submit action or submitted history. Its first generic describes child nodes; nested forms keep their own submission behavior.

GroupApi.usage: Use for structural-group API operations. A group's `$api` combines this contract with a callable signal; child nodes are available through `children`.
GroupApi.description: State and operations for a structural group, including its typed children.

GroupOptions.usage: Use when a structural group needs its own validators or state options. Groups do not accept the form-specific submission workflow. The `configure` callback receives this instance’s typed, collision-safe API synchronously once. See [configuration lifecycle and sibling rules](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md).

GroupPatch.usage: Use to derive the patch value contract from the group's child or item node types. It describes accepted patch input rather than a complete node value. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

GroupSet.usage: Use to derive the replace value contract from the group's child or item node types. It describes the complete value accepted by set(). Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

GroupValue.usage: Use to derive the read value contract from the group's child or item node types. The result describes raw data, not child nodes. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

FormNodesConfig.usage: Use for options passed to [`provideFormNodesConfig()`](../provide-form-nodes-config.md). Injector-scoped values configure bindings and validator messages in that scope.

DisabledReason.usage: Use when presenting or inspecting why a node is disabled. Preserve the originating node information when distinguishing local and inherited causes.

DisabledStateSource.usage: Use when sharing a disabled configuration between declarations. A string supplies a reason; reactive functions participate in state dependency tracking.

DynamicNode.usage: Use when the node kind is unknown but you know child names do not shadow common members. Choose [`AnyNode`](./any-node.md) with `$api` when you cannot make that guarantee.

FormNodeValue.usage: Extract a value type from an existing node with `FormNodeValue<typeof myForm>`. This works across node kinds and avoids repeating the model's value interface.

MarkAsTouchedOptions.usage: Use for reusable wrappers around `markAsTouched()`. `skipDescendants` limits propagation; node interactivity rules still govern whether touching applies.
MarkAsTouchedOptions.description: Options controlling whether markAsTouched() propagates to descendants.

AnyNode.usage: Use for a node of unknown kind or structure. Read state and call operations through `$api`; child names can shadow direct members. Use [`isFormNode()`](../is-form-node.md) to narrow an unknown value to this type.

NodeApi.usage: Use when a helper needs only shared state and operations. This is the API object contract; use [`AnyNode`](./any-node.md) for the node itself and access its `$api`.
NodeApi.description: The common API surface shared by all node kinds.

AsyncValidatorOptions.usage: Use for callback-form async scheduling, activation, and error recovery. Parameterless `when` returns are unchecked for self-reference inference; context-taking conditions retain boolean checking.

ParameterizedAsyncValidatorConfig.usage: Use for the single-object form of `asyncValidator({ params, validate, ... })`. Keep tracked dependency reads in `params` and asynchronous work in `validate`.
ParameterizedAsyncValidatorConfig.description: The object-form asyncValidator configuration, combining reactive params with an asynchronous validate callback.

ParameterizedAsyncValidatorOptions.usage: Use for async options that also derive tracked params. The execution function belongs to [`ParameterizedAsyncValidatorConfig`](./parameterized-async-validator-config.md).

FormFactory.usage: Use when passing the configured form factory from [`createFormPrimitives()`](../create-form-primitives.md) to reusable declaration helpers.
FormFactory.description: The form factory returned by createFormPrimitives().

GroupFactory.usage: Use when passing the configured group factory from [`createFormPrimitives()`](../create-form-primitives.md) to reusable declaration helpers.
GroupFactory.description: The group factory returned by createFormPrimitives().

ArrayFactory.usage: Use when passing the configured array factory from [`createFormPrimitives()`](../create-form-primitives.md) to reusable declaration helpers.
ArrayFactory.description: The array factory returned by createFormPrimitives().

FieldFactory.usage: Use when passing a configured field factory to shared declaration code. Its overloads preserve nullable and strict modes.
FieldFactory.description: A configured field factory with nullable and strict declaration modes.

FormPrimitives.usage: Use for a bundle returned by [`createFormPrimitives()`](../create-form-primitives.md). Keep the configured factories together when sharing defaults across declarations.
FormPrimitives.description: The family of configured field, form, group, and array factories.

FormPrimitivesOptions.usage: Use for the defaults supplied to [`createFormPrimitives()`](../create-form-primitives.md). Per-node declarations can still provide their own options where supported.

NonNullableFieldFactory.usage: Use for a configured factory whose ordinary field declarations exclude null. Its overloads define how explicit nullable choices are represented.
NonNullableFieldFactory.description: A configured field factory whose default declarations exclude null.

ControlState.usage: Use for reusable UI that observes a binding through [`useFormNodeState()`](../form-node-state.md). This read-only facade normalizes supported Angular binding sources and does not expose node write operations.

ControlStateError.usage: Use when rendering errors obtained from [`useFormNodeState()`](../form-node-state.md). This is a source-neutral error contract rather than a guarantee of a Form Nodes target node.

ControlStateSource.usage: Use to inspect which binding API supplies a [`ControlState`](./control-state.md). The source can be absent when no supported binding is available; observe the facade's `source` signal.

ControlStateDisabledReason.usage: Use for disabled explanations from [`useFormNodeState()`](../form-node-state.md). Unlike node-specific [`DisabledReason`](./disabled-reason.md), this contract does not assume the original source is a Form Nodes node.

ValidatorMessages.usage: Use for a partial built-in message catalog supplied through configuration. Omitted entries continue through the normal message-resolution fallbacks.

ValidatorMessageParameters.usage: Use when writing reusable message functions that need built-in structured error data. The selected error kind determines which parameters are available.

FormNodeControl.usage: Use as the union contract when infrastructure accepts either a value-model control or a boolean checkbox-model control. Implement the specific value or checkbox contract in concrete components.

FormNodeUiControl.usage: Use for the optional state inputs and interaction hooks shared by custom controls. It does not by itself supply the required value or checked model.

FormNodeValueControl.usage: Implement this contract in a custom component exposing a `value` model. Match its value type to the bound field, including nullability, and emit `touch` for completed interaction.

FormNodeCheckboxControl.usage: Implement this contract in a custom component exposing a boolean `checked` model. Use a non-nullable boolean field when the component cannot represent null.

ArrayApi.usage: Use for item-management helpers that need array operations. The callable `$api` also preserves the array's `length` signal.
ArrayApi.description: State and operations for an array node, including item access and reconciliation.

ArraySet.usage: Use to derive the replace value contract from the array's child or item node types. It describes the complete value accepted by set(). Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

ArrayNode.usage: Use for dynamic collections whose first generic is the item node type. Read items and use array operations through the inferred API rather than treating this as a JavaScript array of raw values.

ArrayItems.usage: Use for the item-node collection returned by array navigation. These are nodes rather than raw array values.
ArrayItems.description: The typed collection of item nodes exposed by an array node.

ArrayValue.usage: Use to derive the read value contract from the array's child or item node types. The result describes raw data, not child nodes. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

ArrayPatch.usage: Use to derive the patch value contract from the array's child or item node types. It describes accepted patch input rather than a complete node value. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

ArrayIndexes.usage: Use when describing an array node's numeric property access. Each indexed item retains the owning array as its parent.
ArrayIndexes.description: Numeric node access with parent-aware array item types.

ArrayOptions.usage: Use for array initialization and reconciliation options. Keep initial records and options such as `trackBy` together in the array declaration. The `configure` callback receives this instance’s typed, collision-safe API synchronously once. See [configuration lifecycle and sibling rules](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md).
ArrayOptions.description: Template, initial-data, validation, and ownership configuration for array().

ArrayItemWithParent.usage: Use when preserving an array item's navigation relationship in a reusable type. Ordinary consumers should normally let array item access infer it.
ArrayItemWithParent.description: An array item node whose parent is typed as the owning array.

FormNode.usage: Use for inputs and helpers that require form submission semantics. Its generic describes child nodes, not the plain form-value object; use [`FormValueContract`](./form-value-contract.md) for value-oriented constraints.

FormApi.usage: Use for form API operations such as submission without exposing direct child-name collisions. The form's callable `$api` is described by [`CallableNodeApi<FormApi<...>>`](./callable-node-api.md).
FormApi.description: State and operations for a form, including typed children and submission.

FormSet.usage: Use to derive the replace value contract from the form's child or item node types. It describes the complete value accepted by set(). Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

AddedNode.usage: Use when describing the result of a dynamic addition. The resulting node preserves the normalized definition and its new parent type.

FormPatch.usage: Use to derive the patch value contract from the form's child or item node types. It describes accepted patch input rather than a complete node value. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

FormValue.usage: Use to derive the read value contract from the form's child or item node types. The result describes raw data, not child nodes. Use [`FormNodeValue<typeof node>`](./form-node-value.md) when starting from an existing node instance.

FormOptions.usage: Use when sharing form configuration, including `submitWhen`, `onSubmit`, and `onSubmitBlocked`. Let the form declaration infer its concrete value and node callback types when possible. The `configure` callback receives this instance’s typed, collision-safe API synchronously once. See [configuration lifecycle and sibling rules](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md).
FormOptions.description: Value, validation, interaction, ownership, and submission configuration for form().

FormValueContract.usage: Use to check a form or group against an application value shape while preserving its inferred children. It is a structural compatibility contract, not a factory or a replacement node instance.

DynamicFormChildren.usage: Use for runtime-key child iteration when exact property names are unknown. Access each child's `$api` to avoid direct member collisions.

Validator.usage: Use to type a reusable synchronous rule. Author it through [`validator()`](../validator.md) when you want contextual value and owner inference from the consuming declaration.

Validators.usage: Use for a normalized readonly collection of composable rules. Use [`ValidatorSource`](./validator-source.md) for public inputs that also accept a single validator or nullish entries.

ValidatorApi.usage: Use for the generic node API available inside synchronous validator contexts. Supply a more specific owner through the validator's generics only when the consuming contract guarantees it.

FieldContext.usage: Use when a contract specifically requires the low-level reactive field context. Consumer-authored reusable rules normally use [`ValidatorContext`](./validator-context.md) or contextual inference through [`validator()`](../validator.md).

AsyncValidator.usage: Use for the marked result of [`asyncValidator()`](../async-validator.md). A plain function returning a Promise is not a substitute for configuring a validator through the helper.

ValidatorSource.usage:
Use for inputs accepting declaration validator sources. Both parameterless and context-taking declaration callbacks have unchecked returns. The context and node model remain typed.

The internal `DeclarationValidator<TValue, TField>` signature is `(context: ValidatorContext<TValue, ValidatorApi<TValue>, TField>) => any`.

:::info Supported results remain typed contracts

The `any` return avoids circular initializer inference; it does not expand valid runtime results. Return [`ValidationResult`](./validation-result.md) for errors/messages/success, or [`ComposableValidationResult<TValue, TField>`](./composable-validation-result.md) for synchronous composition. Annotate that return or use a context-taking [`validator()`](../validator.md) helper for checked authoring. Returned inline callbacks need such a checked context. See the [full result contract](../../guides/validation.md#validator-results).

:::

ValidationError.usage: Use for the base error category and optional human-readable message. Prefer a targeted error type when consuming a node's error collection.

ValidationErrorForKind.usage: Use to derive the structured error associated with a kind, including registered custom kinds. Its fallback does not prove application-specific properties exist.

ValidationErrorWithTargetNode.usage: Use when consuming errors already associated with a node. The generic preserves the target node type, and binding-specific attribution may also be available.

ValidationErrorWithOptionalTargetNode.usage: Use for infrastructure accepting errors before or after target assignment. Check whether a target exists before using it.

ValidationErrorWithoutTargetNode.usage: Use when returning a rule error for the current node and letting the pipeline assign ownership. Use a targeted contract only when intentionally redirecting the error.

ValidatorError.usage: Use for a validator-returned error with optional target attribution. The pipeline can supply the current node when no explicit target is present.

ValidationStatus.usage: Use to distinguish valid, invalid, and unresolved validation states. Pending asynchronous work does not necessarily make a node invalid; consult the validation-state guide for aggregation.

ValidationResult.usage: Use as an explicit synchronous return annotation to break an inference cycle while preserving checked results. Nullish success, supported messages, and error collections follow the validator contract.

ValidatorContext.usage: Use for a synchronous callback's context. Read its reactive `value` and navigation API rather than assuming a concrete primitive unless the generic supplies one. Use `ctx.parent<TParent>()` for an explicit immediate-parent contract; this is a type assertion with no runtime check and always preserves null and the recursive read-only validation view. Nullish members of the generic are removed automatically, so `ctx.parent<PageForm['roles'][number]>()` needs no `NonNullable` wrapper and returns a node view or null, never undefined. Validation outputs and mutations stay unavailable even with an explicit generic. Prefer [configure](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md) for inferred sibling access.

ValidationSuccess.usage: Use when a rule explicitly reports successful validation. Return the supported success values rather than arbitrary truthy or falsy values.

AsyncValidatorApi.usage: Use for the node API exposed by asynchronous validator contexts. Follow the async validation contract for cancellation and result publication.

ValidationErrorMap.usage: Augment this interface from the package module to register application-specific error kinds. Add a literal `kind` and structured properties so `getError(kind)` can narrow them.

AsyncValidatorState.usage: Use for the state contract available through validator node APIs. Its declaration intentionally avoids recursively depending on the validation state being computed.

ComposableValidator.usage: Use for a synchronous rule that can return another validator or a nested validator collection. Returned compositions retain the validation pipeline's state and error handling.

ValidatorReadonlyApi.usage: Use when a validator integration should depend only on reactive value and navigation. Avoid requiring mutation operations when observation is sufficient.

AsyncValidationResult.usage: Use for the Promise-like or Observable-like result of async validation. It describes the result container; create the validator itself with [`asyncValidator()`](../async-validator.md).

AsyncValidatorContext.usage: Use for an asynchronous validation callback. Observe `abortSignal` and return a supported async result; do not publish stale work after cancellation.

CustomValidationError.usage: Use for unregistered custom errors. Additional data remains unknown; narrow or register the error kind before treating custom properties as concrete types.

BuiltInValidationError.usage: Use when a contract accepts only library-provided error kinds. Narrow by `kind` before reading kind-specific data such as bounds or duplicate indexes.

AsyncValidatorBaseContext.usage: Use for shared async conditions, parameter derivation, and failure handlers. The execution callback adds cancellation and, in parameterized mode, the params snapshot.

ComposableValidationResult.usage: Use for synchronous validator results that may include further validator composition. Use [`ValidationResult`](./validation-result.md) when the rule only returns errors or success.

ParameterizedAsyncValidatorContext.usage: Use for the object-form async validator's execution callback. Its `params` are the captured request snapshot; signal reads in execution are not the parameter dependency declaration.

GlobalFormNodesConfig.usage: Use for [`configureGlobalFormNodes()`](../configure-global-form-nodes.md) defaults. Prefer an injector-scoped provider when configuration must be scoped to an Angular application or subtree.

SyncInputs.usage: Use to configure synchronization on bindings or configured primitives. This chooses synchronized inputs; it does not change the underlying node's validation or state.
SyncInputs.description: Controls which node states and constraints are synchronized to a bound control.

SyncInputName.usage: Use when constructing a typed list of individual synchronized state or constraint names. Pass the list through the appropriate `syncInputs` configuration.
SyncInputName.description: Names accepted when selecting individual synchronized control inputs.

NodeValueSignal.usage: Use when a helper accepts the public `value` facade, including `committed` and `control` reads and setters. Ordinary application value reads can call the node directly.

CallableNodeApi.usage: Use to describe a collision-safe API that is also callable as a signal. Calling it reads the exposed node value; its own members are not replaced by child names.

FormNodeSubmitEvent.usage: Use for template submit and submit-blocked handlers. The generic preserves the bound form and value types; `event` is the original native event, and `form.$api` gives collision-safe access.

NodeErrorsSignal.usage: Use for a node error signal that supports both own and subtree reads. Calling `errors()` retains the owner type; `errors({ descendants: true })` includes descendant targets and matches `allErrors()`.

ArrayItemNode.usage: Extract an existing item node from an already inferred array: `ArrayItemNode<typeof profile.roles>`. Preserves child types and parent navigation while excluding the missing-index `undefined` case. See [configuring sibling rules](../../guides/configuring-nodes.md).
ArrayItemNode.description: The existing item node type of an array node, excluding undefined.

ClosestFormState.usage: Use for shared submission UI built with [`useClosestFormState()`](../use-closest-form-state.md). Its signals normalize Form Nodes, Reactive Forms, and NgForm while retaining optional Form Nodes API access.

ControlError.usage: Use for structured component errors contributed through [`useFormNodeState({ errors })`](../form-node-state.md#contribute-errors). Errors belong to the host binding and cannot target another node.

FormNodeStateOptions.usage: Configure a reactive component-owned error source for [`useFormNodeState()`](../form-node-state.md#contribute-errors). Return an error, a message, a readonly array, or no result.

FormNodeErrorsContext.usage: Context for the projected `#message` template in [`FormNodeErrors`](../form-node-errors.md#custom-template), exposing the first visible message, all visible messages, and their error details.
